steps.speaker: Guard

steps.text: The guard leans in closer and whispers to you.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Sorry about all this. I'm pretty confident you had nothing to do with any of it, but I need to put on a good show for Lady Carnillean.

steps.player: Right...

steps.speaker: Guard

steps.player: Well I'm glad we could...

steps.player: But I never said...

steps.speaker: Guard

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: It happened in the early hours of the morning. According to Lady Carnillean, Sir Ceril heard a noise coming from Butler Jones' old room. He got up to investigate.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: After a few moments, she heard Sir Ceril shout something, followed by a scream. She went to see what was happening, and this is what she found.

steps.player: So no one else was in the room?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Not that she saw.

steps.player: Where was everyone else at this point?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: I was the guard on duty last night. I was stationed out front as usual. Claus, the family chef, was down in the kitchen preparing an early breakfast for Sir Ceril.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Young Philipe was in bed. He slept through the entire thing.

steps.player: Do we have any obvious suspects?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Jones is behind bars, but many of his fellow cultists are still at large. Perhaps this was an act of revenge on their part.

a-death-in-the-family-knocking-at-the-fa.text: If the player helped the cult:

steps.text: The false wall looks to have been slightly damaged.

steps.player: I think that's everything.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: So someone broke in from the outside, something may have been stolen from a hidden room upstairs, and Sir Ceril was stabbed in the back. All useful information, but none of it gives us anything definitive.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Thankfully, we do have one more lead that might hold some promise. Take a look at this.
The guard shows you an amulet with a skull on it.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: I found this by the window. That skull on it is the symbol of the Khazard Army. There's also a name engraved into the back: 'Evelot'.

steps.player: Sounds like we need to find this Evelot and see what they know.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: While I agree, my superiors won't be happy if I open an investigation into a member of the Khazard Army. I think you'll need to handle this bit yourself. Besides, I need to take care of matters here.

steps.player: Right...

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: If you want a place to start, I'd suggest the bar at the Fight Arena. Places like that are always good for gathering information.

steps.player: Good idea.

options.text: Should we not look into the Hazeel Cult as well?

steps.player: Should we not look into the Hazeel Cult as well?

steps.speaker: Guard

steps.player: I see. Fair enough.

options.text: Why can't you investigate the Khazard Army yourself?

steps.player: Why can't you investigate the Khazard Army yourself?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: The matter is... complicated. On paper, General Khazard is an upstanding citizen, and his private army operates with approval from the crown. King Lathas even hired them for some peacekeeping once.

steps.player: But?

steps.text: It's fair to say that Khazard is a bit... controversial. His war with the gnomes is creating more than a few problems for Kandarin, not to mention the rumours about the people fighting in his arena...

steps.player: If you're sure.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Agreed. Did you find anything else?

steps.player: Ceril was stabbed from behind.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: So he wasn't facing his killer. But if that were the case, why did Lady Carnillean say she heard him shouting? Surely he'd have been facing whoever he was shouting at.

steps.text: Let's hope not. One killer on the loose is bad enough.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Do you think they took anything from it?

steps.speaker: Guard

steps.player: I have to go.

steps.text: Well, well, well, what do we have here?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Lord Hazeel, this is the adventurer who killed Alomone and got Jones captured.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: I see. So it was your actions that prevented my followers from bringing about my restoration?

steps.player: Er... I guess so.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: There was once a time when any who dared oppose me would flee to the furthest corners of this world to escape my wrath. Alas, it seems that in my absence, you mortals have grown arrogant once more.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: It is no matter though, for your fate will be a reminder of what happens to those foolish enough to cross a Mahjarrat. Die now, knowing your efforts were in vain, for despite your best attempts, I have returned!

steps.player: Before you go any further, there's something we should discuss.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: And why would I want to discuss anything with you?

steps.player: Because Ceril Carnillean is dead, and his killer may be trying to frame you!

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Dead? How curious. Clivet, I trust this was not our work?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: It was not, my lord.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Very well, adventurer. Speak your piece, but do so quickly. When you are done, I will decide if your life is forfeit.

steps.player: A member of the Khazard Army called Evelot was hired to steal a scroll from the Carnillean Mansion and deliver it here.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: And she was succesful. Thanks to her, my followers were able to use that scroll to bring about my restoration.

steps.player: Well during her escape, Ceril Carnillean was killed, but not by her. Someone else was there, but she doesn't know who.
The evidence I've found so far suggests that the killer was trying to frame her. By extension, they might have been trying to frame you as well.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: You suggest that this individual is my foe, but if that were true, why would they have arranged to have my restoration scroll delivered here?

steps.player: I don't know.

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Whoever this person is, they must be an ally to us, my lord.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: And yet, an ally who hides in darkness is no true ally at all.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Adventurer, you say this Evelot is part of the Khazard Army?

steps.player: That's right.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Then I think it's time to make my return known to my Mahjarrat kin. Clivet, summon Khazard. Let us see what he has to say of this.

steps.player: Er... is now a bad time to mention that Khazard and I have a... complicated history?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Well then, I suggest you prepare yourself.

steps.player: Oh boy...

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Vanar! Septinar! Filinar!

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: Khazard appears before Hazeel, Clivet, and the player.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Hazeel? You've returned?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Surprised, Khazard? Or just disappointed?

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Disappointed? I have no reason to be disappointed.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: And yet you made no attempt to aid me yourself. Too busy claiming my lands as your own, perhaps?

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: They were our lands! And... hang on... what is this human filth doing here?

steps.player: Filth? You're one to talk!

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: It's clear that I've allowed you to endure for far too long! Allow me to correct that mistake.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Enough! This human is no friend of mine either, but [he/she] has presented me with information regarding my return that warrants investigation.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Then kill [him/her] and let's investigate. Or has your sleep made you go soft?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Make no mistake, if the human crosses me, I will gouge out [his/her] eyes and watch as [he/she] dines on them. Until then, [he/she] may be of use.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Fine, but I hope you know this is a foolish idea. What is the information [he/she] presented?

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: If the player helped the cult:

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Welcome, adventurer. It's good to see you once more.

steps.player: Alomone, I need to speak with Hazeel.

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: I'm afraid that isn't possible. Lord Hazeel is currently busy with his glorious work in the north. It is not our place to disturb him.

steps.player: But it's very important. Has Jones not told you what's happened?

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Jones? We have not heard from him in some time.

steps.player: Well then I guess I'll be the one to break the news instead. Ceril Carnillean has been murdered.

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: He has? What joyous news! Long have we waited for those Carnillean monsters to face the consequences of their crimes!

steps.player: I'd hold off on the celebrating if I were you. Something strange is going on and I really need to talk to Hazeel about it.

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Well... I suppose you have proven yourself to be a loyal servant to Hazeel. Still, I must warn you, our lord won't take kindly to being summoned unnecessarily.

steps.player: I understand.

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Very well. I will call upon the mighty Hazeel.

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Vanar! Maradar! Dominar!

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Adventurer, you have summoned me. I trust you understand that my work in the north is of the upmost urgency. I have little time for distractions.

steps.player: I assure you, this is important.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Then speak.

steps.player: A member of the Khazard Army called Evelot was hired to steal your restoration scroll from the Carnillean Mansion. She was meant to deliver it here, but of course, it had already been taken.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: And?

steps.player: During her escape, Ceril Carnillean was killed, but not by her. Someone else was there, but she doesn't know who.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Curious. Alomone, I trust this was not our work?

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Not to my knowledge, my lord. Your loyal servant, Jones, was still stationed at the mansion, but he would not have acted without instruction.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Where is Jones now?

steps.player: He fled after the murder took place. The guards are still searching for him.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: The actions of a coward. He will come to regret that.

steps.player: There's something else as well. The evidence I've found so far suggests that the killer was trying to frame Evelot.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: And you believe they were attempting to frame my followers and I as well?

steps.player: That's what I'm wondering.

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Forgive me, my lord, but if they aimed to frame us, why would they also try to have your restoration scroll delivered here?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: A question with many possible answers, my faithful servant.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Adventurer, you say this Evelot is part of the Khazard Army?

steps.player: That's right.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Then let us see what my Mahjarrat kin has to say about this. Alomone, summon Khazard.

steps.player: Er... is now a bad time to mention that Khazard and I have a... complicated history?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Well then, I suggest you prepare yourself.

steps.player: Oh boy...

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Vanar! Septinar! Filinar!

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: Khazard appears before Hazeel, Alomone, and the player.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Hazeel? What is the meaning of this? And what is this human filth doing here?

steps.player: Filth? You're one to talk!

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: It's clear that I've allowed you to endure for far too long! Allow me to correct that mistake.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Enough! I care not for your petty disagreements. This adventurer is under my protection. You are not to harm [him/her].

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Has the once great Hazeel gone soft? Never would I have expected you to work with scum like this. I trust you know that [he'll/she'll] betray you?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: And if [he/she] does, I will gouge out [his/her] eyes and watch as [he/she] dines on them. Until then, cease this prattle.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Fine, but I hope you have good reason for this.

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.speaker: Hazeel
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: Someone has murdered Ceril Carnillean and attempted to pass the blame onto one of your minions. Were you aware of this?

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.speaker: General Khazard
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: I don't involve myself in the personal affairs of my soldiers. Besides, I'd have thought you'd be happy to see that fool dead.

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.speaker: Hazeel
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: I shed no tears for his demise, and if his killer turns out to be a friend, I will reward them with riches beyond imagination. However, this individual and their motives remain unknown. We must rectify that.

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.speaker: General Khazard
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: Bah! This matter is beneath the both of us. Accept this for the gift it is and move on.

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.speaker: Hazeel
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: No. Any individual involving themselves in our affairs, be they friend or foe, must be made known to us, especially as the ritual draws near.

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.speaker: Hazeel
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: Adventurer, how thorough has the investigation into Ceril Carnillean's murder been?

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.player: I'd say it's been pretty thorough. I handled most of it myself.

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.speaker: Hazeel
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: No stone can be left unturned. Adventurer, you must return to the Carnillean Mansion and uncover any information you might have missed.

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.speaker: General Khazard
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: You're trusting [him/her] with this? Stop this madness and let me handle it instead.

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.speaker: Hazeel
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-alomone.text: This is not up for debate. I have made my will clear. Return to us once you have something, adventurer. Not before.

steps.player: Why should I help you?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: You came to me, not the other way around. From that, I would assume that you already have some sort of motive in finding this killer. I care not what that motive is.

steps.player: Aren't you worried about my loyalties?

steps.text: If the player opposed the cult:

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Loyalty means very little to my kind. You opposed me before, but now you have a chance to rectify that mistake. Do so, and you will be rewarded. Oppose me again, and you will die.
If the player helped the cult:

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Loyalty means very little to my kind. Still, without you, I might never have been awoken from my slumber.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Continue to support me and you will continue to be rewarded. The moment you oppose me, however, is the moment you die.

options.text: Can you think of any possible suspects?

steps.player: Can you think of any possible suspects?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Thousands. To have lived as long as I is to have made many friends, and many enemies. Any one of them may be responsible. Without further information, it is pointless to speculate.

options.text: What is this ritual you mentioned?

steps.player: What is this ritual you mentioned?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: It is nothing you need to concern yourself with.

steps.player: The more information I have, the more help I can be.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: You can be of ample help by performing the task you've been assigned. This idle chatter achieves nothing.

steps.player: I'll be on my way.

on-the-trail-talking-to-alomone-after-he.speaker: Alomone
on-the-trail-talking-to-alomone-after-he.text: Adventurer, I have summoned the mighty Hazeel as you desired. You should speak with him at once.

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-after-he-.speaker: Hazeel
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-after-he-.text: Adventurer, you have summoned me. I trust you understand that my work in the north is of the upmost urgency. I have little time for distractions.

on-the-trail-talking-to-alomone-after-he.speaker: Alomone
on-the-trail-talking-to-alomone-after-he.text: Adventurer, you should speak with Lord Hazeel and General Khazard at once.

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-or-genera.speaker: General Khazard
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-or-genera.text: Hazeel? What is the meaning of this? And what is this human filth doing here?

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Lord Hazeel has given you a task to perform. Go and get it done.

on-the-trail-talking-to-clivet-alomone.text: If the player helped the cult:

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Lord Hazeel has given you a task to perform. You should go with haste.

on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-after-he-.speaker: Hazeel
on-the-trail-talking-to-hazeel-after-he-.text: Adventurer, you have work to do. Go to the Carnillean Mansion and uncover any information you might have missed. Return to us once you have something. Not before.

options.text: Can you think of any possible suspects?
What is this ritual you mentioned?
Can you think of any possible suspects?

steps.player: Can you think of any possible suspects?

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: No.

steps.player: None at all?

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: No. Now go away.

options.text: You and Hazeel seem to have some history.

steps.player: You and Hazeel seem to have some history.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Continue to bother me and I'll make you history. Now go away.

steps.player: Nothing.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Then go away.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.player: Hello. I'd like to ask you some questions about what happened.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.text: Please, leave me. If you have questions, take them to the guard outside.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-phi.player: Hello there. I'd like to ask you some questions about your dad.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-phi.speaker: Philipe Carnillean
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-phi.text: I shouldn't talk to you. You might be one of the bad people. The guard said I should be careful of the bad people.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.player: Hello there. I'd like to ask you some questions.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.speaker: Claus the Chef
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.text: I don't know if I should be answering any questions. You should probably check with the guard first.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-the.speaker: Guard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-the.text: Hello there. Any luck at the Fight Arena?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-the.player: I think so. I found Evelot and was able to question her. It seems someone might be trying to frame her.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-the.text: If the player opposed the cult:

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Interesting. So what do you plan to do now?

steps.player: I'd like to have another look around and ask some questions.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-the.text: If the player helped the cult:

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Well you'll be pleased to know we were able to track down Jones. He's already admitted to being part of that cult. For that alone he'll be going away for a long time. However, he's staying silent on the murder.

steps.player: To be honest, with what I've discovered so far, I don't think he was involved. I suspect he just fled out of fear.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Really? He seems like the obvious suspect. If not him, then who?

steps.player: That's what I'm here to find out. I'd like to have another look around and ask some questions.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-the.speaker: Guard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-the.text: Go right ahead. Lady Carnillean and Philipe are just inside, and you'll find Claus down in the kitchen.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.player: Hello. I'd like to ask you some questions about what happened.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.text: You're the one my husband hired to deal with that cult. Some good that did!

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.player: I'm sorry, but right now we don't even think the cult were responsible.
That's what I'm hoping to find out.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.text: Fine. What do you want to know?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.player: When your husband was killed, did you see anything unusual?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.text: No. It's as I told the guard. There was a noise coming from Jones' old room. My husband went to take a look and I heard him shout something.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.player: Did you hear what he shouted?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.text: I didn't. I went to see what was happening, and I heard a scream. By the time I arrived, the only one there was my husband, lying on the floor.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-hen.player: And there was nothing else in the room that seemed odd?
Okay, thank you for your help.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-phi.player: Hello there. I'd like to ask you some questions about your dad.
Did you see any of what happened?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-phi.speaker: Philipe Carnillean
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-phi.text: No! I was in bed. Now leave me alone! I don't want to talk to you.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-phi.player: Okay, I'm sorry to have bothered you.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.player: Hello there. I'd like to ask you some questions.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.speaker: Claus the Chef
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.text: But I already spoke to the authorities earlier.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.player: I know, but I'm hoping I can uncover anything they missed.
What were you doing at the time Ceril Carnillean was killed?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.speaker: Claus the Chef
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.text: I was here in the kitchen. Sir Ceril is an early riser, and he likes a good breakfast as soon as he wakes up.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.player: And you didn't see anything unusual down here?
You're absolutely sure? Not even the slightest thing out of place?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.speaker: Claus the Chef
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.text: Well... no... not really. I guess there was the cold...

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.speaker: Claus the Chef
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.text: Yes... this sudden cold feeling. I was right next to the warm stove, so it was very odd. I thought it was just some wind... but maybe...

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.player: Did you see anything when you felt this cold?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.speaker: Claus the Chef
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.text: Well... I thought I saw this shadow in the room, just for a moment. Surely it was just a trick of the light though...

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.player: Hmm... I'm going to have a little look around down here, if that's okay?
I'm still working on it. Could you describe exactly what you felt and saw again?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.speaker: Claus the Chef
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.text: There was this sudden cold feeling and when I turned around, I thought I saw a shadow. Surely it was just a trick of the light...

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.player: If it was anything important, I'll find it.

the-mysterious-benefactor-reading-the-sc.player: Interesting... I wonder what Hazeel will make of this.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-the.text: Hello there. Any luck with your investigation?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-the.player: I have a new lead that I'm exploring.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-the.speaker: Guard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-the.text: Excellent. I hope it goes well.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cla.player: I think so. Hopefully it can help me find the killer.

steps.text: Have you completed your task? Speak with Lord Hazeel and General Khazard if so.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cli.text: If the player helped the cult:

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Adventurer, is your task complete? You should speak with Lord Hazeel and General Khazard if so.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: The adventurer returns. I trust this means you have something of note for us.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.player: I found a hidden room beneath the Carnillean Mansion. There was a chest inside with a scroll in it.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: A scroll?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.player: Yes. It had a sketch on it of some sort of crest. Well... half of one, at least.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Half a crest? Could that be...?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: This chest, was there nothing else inside?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: The crest must have been in there.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: So that was their true target. But I thought it was lost... How did it get there?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: The Carnilleans must have claimed it after my defeat. The fools would have had no idea of its importance.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Who would even want to steal that thing? One of our kin, perhaps?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Quite possibly, though there are others who would know of it.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.player: Are you two going to keep talking in riddles, or are you going to tell me what's going on?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Something is still amiss in all of this.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: I agree, but our next move is clear. We must go north.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.player: Maybe I've discovered the ability to turn totally invisible.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: We should not waste any time. However, we must first deal with the human.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: I will handle it.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Adventurer, your work is done. Leave us.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.player: What? But we haven't found the killer.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: If the player opposed the cult:

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Khazard and I will deal with this matter now. As a reward for your work, consider your past transgressions against us forgiven. Now go.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: If the player helped the cult:

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Khazard and I will deal with this matter now. Once again, you have proven yourself a worthy ally to my followers and I. Now go.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: A group of ice trolls have made their home near the fortress. I will join you there.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.player: Ice trolls? Do you mean the trolls at Weiss?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Why are you still here?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Hold on. Adventurer, you know of these trolls and their lands?

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.player: Oh yes, I'm quite good friends with them. You see, there's this troll called My Arm...

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Nobody cares! Be gone from our sight.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: If the human knows these ice trolls, [he/she] may still be of use to us.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Why? We can make short work of any trolls that disturb us. We have no need for dead weight.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Until we know more about who we are dealing with, we should avoid attracting unneeded attention.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Enough of this nonsense! If you want subtlety, we can use the Shadow Realm.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: There are others who dwell in the Shadow Realm. I would prefer they be kept unaware of our presence in the north.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: General Khazard
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Fine, but on your head be it if this goes wrong.
If the player opposed the cult:

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Adventurer, it seems we have further need of you after all. Meet us outside this troll settlement. Don't make us wait.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: If the player helped the cult:

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Alomone, in our absence, I trust you can take care of that matter we spoke of.

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: It will be done, my lord.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Good. Now, adventurer, it seems we have further need of you after all. Meet us outside this troll settlement. Don't make us wait.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Hazeel and Khazard teleport away.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.speaker: Hazeel
the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-haz.text: Adventurer, your work is done. Leave us.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cli.text: If the player opposed the cult:

steps.speaker: Clivet
steps.text: Lord Hazeel and General Khazard require you in the north. Meet with them at the troll settlement there. Now be gone.

the-mysterious-benefactor-talking-to-cli.text: If the player helped the cult:

steps.speaker: Alomone
steps.text: Adventurer, Lord Hazeel and General Khazard require your presence in the north. You should join with them at the troll settlement there.

in-the-north-talking-to-my-arm-or-snowfl.speaker: Snowflake
in-the-north-talking-to-my-arm-or-snowfl.text: Thank you for getting our herb patches to work. Now Boulder can grow goutweed for my people, and they are very happy.

options.text: Can I have another copy of that book?
I'm meant to be meeting some... friends... Have you seen them?

steps.player: I'm meant to be meeting some... friends... Have you seen them?

steps.speaker: Snowflake
steps.text: I don't think so... The only newcomers we've had here recently are those two strange trolls outside. I hope they're not up to no good.

steps.player: Hmm... okay.

options.text: Can you note this basalt for me?

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Good, you're here.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Dead Wolf
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: The idiot doesn't even know it's us.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.player: Wait... Hazeel? Khazard? Why are you trolls?

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Given the secrecy of our task here, we felt it appropriate to shapeshift into less conspicuous forms.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: We? This foolish idea was yours alone.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.player: Right... So what are we doing here?

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Based on your discovery, it is likely our mysterious killer will have travelled here.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.player: To Weiss? What would they want with the trolls?

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Ha! They will have no interest in trolls.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: This troll settlement is a relatively new addition to the area. It is what was here before that will be of interest to the killer.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Which is none of your business. Now, can we get to work?

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Indeed. Adventurer, while our disguises will work up to a point, I imagine any troll would soon see through them if we were to converse with them.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: I doubt that. Trolls are as dumb as they come.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Our first step here is to gather information. As you claim to be friends with these trolls, you will be well placed to do so.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Speak with their leader and find out if anything of note has occurred here recently.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Adventurer, speak with the leader of these trolls and find out if anything of note has occurred here recently. That will determine our next move.

in-the-north-talking-to-other-trolls-aft.speaker: Note
in-the-north-talking-to-other-trolls-aft.text: The same dialogue is shared by Root, Icicle, Driftwood, Goat Poo, Pebble, Yellow Snow, Squirrel, and Boulder.

options.text: Have you seen anything odd around here recently?

steps.player: Have you seen anything odd around here recently?

steps.speaker: [Troll]
steps.text: Odd? Don't think so. Maybe you ask Snowflake and My Arm though?

options.text: Have you seen anything odd around here recently?

steps.player: Have you seen anything odd around here recently?

steps.speaker: Odd Stone
steps.text: Odd? Well my name Odd Stone. Got named after some odd stone thing I found in snowfields south of Weiss.

steps.player: An odd stone thing?

steps.speaker: Odd Stone
steps.text: Yeah, it were made of stone, and it were odd. Some weird bone-head human saw me trying to nibble it, an' he got really upset an' chased me away. He kinda scary.

steps.speaker: Odd Stone
steps.text: Anyway, my parents, they named me Odd Stone after that, and now we trolls not go anywhere near the place. Bone-head human was, like, really scary! And probably magic.

steps.player: A magic person with a bone-head? Interesting... Has anything happened with this stone recently?

steps.speaker: Odd Stone
steps.text: No. We trolls blocked all routes to snowfields from here, but we keep eye out just in case. No bone-head human out there in ages.

steps.player: Hmm... Probably not what I'm after then. Seen anything else odd?

steps.speaker: Odd Stone
steps.text: Don't think so. Maybe you ask Snowflake and My Arm though?

in-the-north-talking-to-my-arm-or-snowfl.speaker: Snowflake
in-the-north-talking-to-my-arm-or-snowfl.text: Thank you for getting our herb patches to work. Now Boulder can grow goutweed for my people, and they are very happy.

options.text: Can I have another copy of that book?
Have you seen anything odd around here recently?

steps.player: Have you seen anything odd around here recently?

steps.speaker: Snowflake
steps.text: Odd? Like what?

steps.player: I'm not sure to be honest. Anything unusual I guess.

steps.speaker: Snowflake
steps.text: Well there's two strange trolls outside who I'm sure I haven't seen before. I hope they're not up to no good.

steps.player: Ah yes... those two. I was speaking to them earlier. They're harmless... I hope.

steps.speaker: My Arm
steps.text: If you want unusual, Goat Poo says he see da weirdness down in mine.

steps.player: Weirdness? What kind of weirdness?

steps.speaker: My Arm
steps.text: He say he see da strange shadow.

steps.speaker: Snowflake
steps.text: There was the cave-in recently down there as well. That's what Goat Poo was investigating when he saw the shadow.

steps.player: Interesting. I think my... companions... might want to hear about this.

options.text: Can you note this basalt for me?

in-the-north-talking-to-my-arm-or-snowfl.speaker: Snowflake
in-the-north-talking-to-my-arm-or-snowfl.text: Thank you for getting our herb patches to work. Now Boulder can grow goutweed for my people, and they are very happy.

options.text: Can I have another copy of that book?
Have you seen anything odd around here recently?

steps.player: Have you seen anything odd around here recently?

steps.speaker: My Arm
steps.text: Did you find da weirdness down in mine?

steps.player: I haven't looked yet.

steps.speaker: Snowflake
steps.text: Goat Poo was investigating the cave-in down there when he says he saw a shadow. Could be worth a look.

steps.player: I'll see what my... companions... think.

options.text: Can you note this basalt for me?

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: We're blind here. My senses do nothing this close to the ritual marker.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Nor mine, but there is no alternative.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: We wouldn't have this problem if we were in the Shadow Realm!

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.player: What are you two on about now?

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Nothing! Stop eavesdropping!

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.player: It's hardly eavesdropping if you're having the conversation right in front of me.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Adventurer, did you discover anything?

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.player: I did, but before we go any further, I think it's time for some answers.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: You're in no place to make demands!

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.player: Well maybe I just won't tell you what I've learnt.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: You waste time we may not have, adventurer, but very well. Ask your questions, but do so quickly.

options.text: Okay, I'm done asking questions. What now?
options.condition: If the player has asked both questions:

steps.player: I'm done asking questions. What now?

steps.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
steps.text: Now you tell us what you have discovered.

steps.player: There's been a cave-in down in the mine. One of the trolls apparently saw a strange shadow near it.

steps.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
steps.text: A shadow? Could just be troll superstition.

steps.player: The cook at the Carnillean Mansion also mentioned seeing a shadow. That doesn't feel like a coincidence.

steps.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
steps.text: It sounds like we should investigate for ourselves. Adventurer, meet us down in this mine.
Hazeel and Khazard depart.

options.text: Why would the killer come here?

steps.player: Why would the killer come here?

steps.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
steps.text: Before the God Wars, a settlement of the old empire was found here. The fortress to the east is all that remains on the surface, but there is much still hidden below.

steps.player: Like what?

steps.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
steps.text: A great prison, sealed long ago. Half of the crest used to do so came into my possession, but it was seemingly taken by the Carnilleans after my defeat.

steps.player: And the killer stole it from the Carnilleans? You think they mean to open the prison?

steps.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
steps.text: That is our assumption.

steps.player: Where's the other half of the crest?

steps.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
steps.text: It was held by one of our kin, but we haven't felt his presence for some time. It's possible the killer already has it.

steps.player: But why would someone want to open this prison? What's inside?

steps.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
steps.text: You've been told enough, human. Finish your questions and let us get back to work.

options.text: What is this ritual you keep talking about?

steps.player: What is this ritual you keep talking about?

steps.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
steps.text: What do you know of our kind?

steps.player: The Mahjarrat? Not a lot to be honest.

steps.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
steps.text: Then let's keep it that way. This question has no relevance to our purpose here, Hazeel. It doesn't warrant an answer.

steps.player: If it's not relevant, why do you two keep talking about it?

steps.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
steps.text: It may be relevant, it may not be. It depends on who this killer is.

steps.player: Well assuming it is relevant, what can you tell me about it?

steps.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
steps.text: The ritual is used by our kind to ensure our survival, and the next one is fast approaching. If the killer is one of our kin, their actions may be a means of preparing for it.

steps.player: Preparing how?

steps.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
steps.text: For the rest of us to live, one of us must die. Many will go to great lengths to ensure they are not the one who is sacrificed.

steps.speaker: Dead Wolf (General Khazard)
steps.text: That's enough! You've already shared too much.

steps.player: I have to go.

steps.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
steps.text: We have work to do, adventurer. Don't be gone too long.

in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.speaker: Big Fish (Hazeel)
in-the-north-talking-to-big-fish-or-dead.text: Ask your questions, adventurer, but do so quickly.

options.text: Okay, I'm done asking questions. What now?
options.condition: If the player has asked both questions:

options.text: Why would the killer come here?
What is this ritual you keep talking about?

in-the-north-entering-the-salt-mine.player: Hmm... did Hazeel and Khazard already go inside?

steps.text: Cutscene begins. The player arrives at a dungeon. Secrets of the North plays.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Is this it?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: It is.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Then let's get to work. First, you can't deny this time that the human is of no further use to us.

steps.player: I am here, you know?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Again with this, Khazard? [He/She] has been of great benefit so far. As long as that continues, [he/she] will remain.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: And what if I disagree?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: The decision is already made.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: Says who? You? You don't command me! Do you think you're my lord? Or maybe you think you're my father?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: No, and let us thank Zamorak for that.

steps.player: Hey, stop arguing and listen! I heard something.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Adventurer, let us investigate. Khazard, stay here and guard the entrance.

steps.speaker: General Khazard
steps.text: No. I'll go with the human. You wait here.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Very well.
The player and Khazard walk towards an assassin attempting to open a strange barrier.

steps.player: What the... you!

steps.text: The player and Khazard begin fighting the assassin. In the Shadows plays.

in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.speaker: General Khazard
in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.text: No. Just some cheap parlour trick. He's likely still nearby.

in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.speaker: General Khazard
in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.text: We should, but first, you have some explaining to do. You knew him.

in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.player: Well 'knew' is a bit of a strong word, but we've crossed paths.
I encountered him on Entrana. He killed some monks there and stole a relic from them. I... may have been responsible for helping him, but I didn't realise until it was too late.

in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.speaker: General Khazard
in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.text: Ah, so you were always a fool?

in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.player: You're one to talk. So what was he doing here?

in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.speaker: General Khazard
in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.text: And there you go aptly proving my point. As it seems I have to explain everything, this door leads to the prison Hazeel spoke of earlier.

in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.speaker: General Khazard
in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.text: Your friend is likely the culprit in our little murder mystery, or at least, is working with the one responsible.

in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.player: But it didn't look like he could open the door. He must still only have half the crest.

in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.speaker: General Khazard
in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin.text: And let us hope it stays that way. Now, I will stay here and guard the door in case your friend returns. Go and tell Hazeel what happened. Now.

in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin-talk.speaker: General Khazard
in-the-north-defeating-the-assassin-talk.text: Why are you here? Go and tell Hazeel what happened. Now.

in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.player: He's back there. There's been a development.
We found the door to the prison, and we found someone trying to open it.
An assassin. I've encountered them before, but I don't really know anything about them.
It seems they still only have half of it.

in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.speaker: Hazeel
in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.text: Curious. Why would they come here with only half the crest?

in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.player: Perhaps they didn't know they'd need the other half?

in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.speaker: Hazeel
in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.text: Possible, but unlikely. It should be clear to anyone that both halves are needed. I wonder...

in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.speaker: Hazeel
in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.text: As I mentioned earlier, the other half was held by one of my kin. My kind have the ability to sense each other, but we have not felt his presence for a long time now.

in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.speaker: Hazeel
in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.text: That was my initial assumption, but it is unusual that we have not felt his passing either. It's possible he is masking his presence instead.

in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.speaker: Hazeel
in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.text: It's no easy feat, but it can be done. As fate would have it, we stand in a place where our senses mean nothing.

in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.speaker: Hazeel
in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.text: While foolish to do so, he would have good reason to hide himself in this area.

in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.player: So the other half might be closer than we think. What do we do?

in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.speaker: Hazeel
in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.text: This assassin must be found. I will remain here and ensure no one enters or leaves. You will search the rest of this dungeon and see what you can find.

options.text: Why would this other Mahjarrat hide himself here?

steps.player: Why would this other Mahjarrat hide himself here?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Our rejuvenation ritual takes place right above us. There have been times in the past when the weaker of our number have tried to hide themselves nearby.

steps.player: Why?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: To claim power from the ritual without the risk of being chosen as the sacrifice.

steps.player: So I'm guessing this other Mahjarrat is quite a weak one then?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: You are correct. When the Empty Lord fell, he was one of the few foolish enough to remain loyal. His decision not to join Lord Zamorak left him with few friends. He has slowly grown weak ever since.

options.text: What's inside the prison that the assassin would want?

steps.player: What's inside the prison that the assassin would want?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: The prison was sealed long ago by two of my traitorous kin. They did so to prevent a great horror from escaping, but it is believed by some that a powerful artefact was also sealed inside.

steps.player: And the assassin wants this artefact?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Most likely. However, his attempts to claim it will risk unleashing what lies within.

steps.player: Which you consider to be a problem?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: In an ideal world, I would see this artefact claimed in the name of Zamorak. But to risk unleashing an abomination of the Fallen Empire when the ritual is so close would not be wise.

options.text: What's the history between you and Khazard?

steps.player: What's the history between you and Khazard?

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: That is none of your business. I have been generous enough to share a great deal of information with you so far, but I will not allow you to pry into personal matters.

steps.player: Fair enough. Could you at least tell him to leave me alone? I feel like every time I turn my back, he's going to put his sword through it.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: And have I not already been stopping him from doing so? Besides, his anger is not without cause. You wronged him, did you not?
If the player opposed the cult:

steps.player: In my defence, he was doing some pretty nasty things. Not to mention, I also wronged you and you're not trying to have me killed constantly.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Yes, but you would be wise not to mistake my mercy for weakness. I am willing to forgive you for your past transgressions as I believe you can be of use.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: However, if I come to regret my choice, your fate will make the fires of Infernus seem welcoming in comparison.
If the player helped the cult:

steps.player: In my defence, he was doing some pretty nasty things.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: If you do not have the stomach for certain... unpleasantries, you should not have allied yourself with me, either.

steps.player: You seem more reasonable than Khazard, though.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Perhaps, but I trust you do not mistake that for weakness. If you wrong me, your fate will make the fires of Infernus seem welcoming in comparison.

steps.player: I'll get going.

in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.speaker: Hazeel
in-the-north-talking-to-hazeel-after-def.text: Adventurer, we must find the assassin. Search the rest of this dungeon and see what you can find.

options.text: Why would this other Mahjarrat hide himself here?
What's inside the prison that the assassin would want?
What's the history between you and Khazard?

in-the-north-talking-to-khazard-after-re.player: I wanted to ask you something.

in-the-north-talking-to-khazard-after-re.speaker: General Khazard
in-the-north-talking-to-khazard-after-re.text: No. I assume Hazeel has given you a job to do? Go get it done and leave me in peace.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-leaving-the.prompt: Are you sure you want to leave?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.speaker: Hazeel
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.text: Adventurer, have you found the assassin?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.player: No, but I have found something... It's sort of hard to explain. I think I need to get back there.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Jhallan
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: Aargh... Muspah! Wait... What...?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Jhallan
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: Hmm... just another nightmare.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.player: Just a nightmare? That feels like a bit of an understatement.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Jhallan
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: What is this? A human?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Jhallan
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: Who are you, human? Speak now, and do so with haste, for you stand before the mighty Jhallan!

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.player: Well I'm [player name], and I'm guessing you're the Mahjarrat I'm looking for.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Jhallan
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: A human, seeking a Mahjarrat? Why? What would a meaningless being like you want with me?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.player: You have half a crest, right? There's an assassin who's after it. I'm trying to stop him.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Jhallan
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: You know of the Ghorrock Crest? How?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Jhallan
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: A story of lies, no doubt. I don't know how you came to stand before me, human, but you are clearly no friend of mine. Leave now, before I bring down the might of the Ruinous Powers on you!

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.player: Wait! It's true! This assassin is nearby. He'll be coming for you!

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Jhallan
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: Then let him come! I am a faithful servant of the Empty Lord. I will not be intimidated by a pathetic human like you.
The assassin appears.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Jhallan
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: And who are you?
The assassin casts a spell and teleports him and Jhallan away.
The player runs to Khazard back at the strange barrier.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.player: Khazard... we have a big problem!

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: General Khazard
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: What have you done now?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.player: I found Jhallan, but the assassin captured him!

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: General Khazard
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: Jhallan was here? Great. Hazeel!
Hazeel appears.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Hazeel
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: What is it?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Hazeel
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: Then he now has everything he needs to enter the prison.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: General Khazard
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: What's our next...

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: General Khazard
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: Hang on...
The strange barrier disappears.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: General Khazard
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: What a mess.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.player: I don't understand. I didn't even see anything.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: General Khazard
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: It seems your friend has quite the range of abilities. He used the Shadow Realm.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.player: So he got inside? Do we follow him?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Hazeel
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: No good will come out of going in there. We have failed.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.player: So we're not going to do anything?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Hazeel
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: Guards will need positioning here to warn us if this assassin remerges. Until then, we can only hope that he meets a swift end in the prison.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: General Khazard
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: I can have a detachment of soldiers despatched here at once. We'll need to keep things light to ensure the trolls don't notice our work. Not to mention our kin...

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Hazeel
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: Still a prisoner of this assassin, no doubt. To what end, who can say.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.player: Is there really nothing else we can do?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Hazeel
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: No. Word will be sent to you if there are any developments, but for now, you should leave. I suggest you return to the authorities in Ardougne and inform them that their killer will not be found.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.player: But there's still so many unanswered questions!

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Hazeel
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: And perhaps one day they will be answered, but to dwell on them now achieves nothing.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: General Khazard
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: We should get to work.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.speaker: Hazeel
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.text: Agreed. Adventurer, we are done here. If you wish, I can provide you with a teleport to Ardougne.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-defeating-t.prompt: Teleport to East Ardougne? You can only use this teleport once.

steps.player: Alright.

steps.text: Hazeel teleports the player.

steps.player: I'll make my own way.

steps.speaker: Hazeel
steps.text: Very well.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.speaker: Hazeel
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.text: Adventurer, we are done here. If you wish, I can provide you with a teleport to Ardougne.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.prompt: Teleport to East Ardougne? You can only use this teleport once.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.speaker: Hazeel
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.text: Adventurer, we are done here. You should return to Ardougne.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.speaker: Guard
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.text: You're back. Any luck with your investigation?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.player: I wish I had better news, but I'm afraid I reached a dead end.
The killer was an assassin. I don't know his true identity, but I previously encountered him on Entrana. He killed some monks there and stole an important relic.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.speaker: Guard
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.text: An assassin? Why would an assassin want Sir Ceril dead?

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.player: Quite a bit is still unclear, but it seems he cared less about killing Ceril and more about recovering something hidden in the mansion.
Somewhere we have no hope of reaching him. Hopefully that changes, but for now, there's not much we can do.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.text: If the player opposed the cult:

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Well I guess I'd better go and file my report on all this. My superiors aren't going to be happy.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Still, thank you for all your help. Even though we weren't successful, I very much appreciate you trying. If you discover anything new about this assassin, do let me know.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.text: If the player helped the cult:

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Well I guess I'd better go and file my report on all this. My superiors aren't going to be happy. First the Jones situation, now this.

steps.player: Jones situation?

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Ah, of course, you don't know. Jones was found dead in his cell. Poison by the looks of it.

steps.player: Oh my!

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Yes, quite the mess. Assumption is the cult are to blame. Tying up loose ends and all that.

steps.speaker: Guard
steps.text: Anyway, thank you for all your help. Even though we weren't successful, I still very much appreciate it. If you discover anythiing new about this assassin, do let me know.

more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.speaker: Guard
more-mahjarrat-more-problems-talking-to-.text: I'll let you be on your way. All the best out there.

post-quest-talking-to-the-guard-post-que.player: Hello there. How are things here?

post-quest-talking-to-the-guard-post-que.speaker: Guard
post-quest-talking-to-the-guard-post-que.text: Things aren't easy for the family, especially since they never got closure. They're getting through it, though.

post-quest-talking-to-the-guard-post-que.player: That's good to hear. Hopefully there's still a chance that the assassin is found one day.

post-quest-talking-to-the-guard-post-que.speaker: Guard
post-quest-talking-to-the-guard-post-que.text: We can hope. If you do ever hear any more about him, be sure to let us know.

post-quest-talking-to-the-guard-post-que.player: Will do. Now, I should leave you to your work.

post-quest-talking-to-philipe-carnillean.speaker: Philipe Carnillean
post-quest-talking-to-philipe-carnillean.text: I don't want to talk to you.

post-quest-talking-to-henryeta-carnillea.speaker: Henryeta Carnillean
post-quest-talking-to-henryeta-carnillea.text: Please, do not disturb me. The loss of my husband is a hard burden to bear. I would prefer not to have distractions.

post-quest-talking-to-claus-the-chef-pos.speaker: Claus the Chef
post-quest-talking-to-claus-the-chef-pos.text: Things aren't the same here now that Sir Ceril is gone.

olnIpJ.player: I think I've seen everything I need to. I should check in with the guard.
